shortDescription: German power prices traded higher for next week as low renewable output is expected and dry conditions continue to reduce output at French nuclear power plants.

children: German power prices traded higher for next week as low renewable output is expected and dry conditions continue to reduce output at French nuclear power plants.
The German Monday baseload contract (TRDEBD3) was at €127.50 per megawatt-hour at 0809 GMT, up 5.8% from the price paid Friday for Monday delivery, LSEG data showed.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBD1) was untraded, according to LSEG data.
Wind conditions should weaken in Germany at the beginning of next week and remain low in France and Spain, increasing upward pressure on spot prices, EnergyScan analysts said.
Dry conditions are also expected to persist with no significant rainfall forecast, raising risks of outages at French nuclear plants due to low water levels, EnergyScan said.
The St Alban 1 reactor is expected to trim production by about 1 GW on Saturday due to environmental issues, while the Bugey 2 is completely offline until Monday, operator EDF data showed.
The Golfech 1 reactor is expected to remain offline until Sept. 27 while the Chooz 1 and 2 reactors remain offline until the start of October, the data showed.
German wind supply is expected to rise by 5.1 gigawatts to 29.2 GW on Monday, before falling throughout the rest of the week, the data showed.
This has helped push front-week prices higher, with the German week-ahead contract (TRDEBWKD1) closing at €179.50/MWh on Thursday.
On the forward side, the German year-ahead baseload contract (TRDEBYc1) rose 0.8% to €128.85/MWh, the data showed.
The rest of the German forward curve was also up in early trading, with most front-quarter and front-month contracts trading at over €170/MWh. (0#TRDEBc)
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBYc1) was untraded with a bid price at €83/MWh, LSEG data showed.
